text.p: These are some of the leading stories in Israeli newspapers on Thursday. Reuters has not verified these stories and does not vouch for their accuracy.
JERUSALEM POST
- Cabinet approves 164 billion shekel 1998 budget.
- U.S. peace envoy Ross: We have a beginning.
- British hitchhiker slain near Eilat.
- U.S. official: Bombers came from abroad.
- Religious Affairs Ministry prints Jewish prayerbook leaving out prayer for welfare of state.
- Arison Group mulls response to Hapoalim delay; group will meet later in week to determine its response to MI Holdings decision to push back date for completing tender proceedings for Hapoalim sale.
- Government narrowly approves budget cut.
HAARETZ
- The government approves economic plan targets.
- Before Israeli Arab group left for Syria, Prime Minister Netanyahu's political adviser met with member of delegation, emphasising Israel interested in renewing peace negotiations.
- After four years, new leader of Israeli Druze named.
- Killing of British tourist and wounding of his girlfriend being investigated along both criminal and nationalist lines.
- Dramatic rise in pollution in France.
YEDIOTH AHRONOTH
- Ministers protest against budget cut, but vote for it.
- Hotel to provide services to Netanyahu family when it vacations at private villa.
- Nazi criminals enjoy higher payments than Holocaust survivors, German government report shows.
- Son of minor Israeli celebrity today meets President Clinton.
- Koor in contacts to join Globes group.
MAARIV
- Budget and economic changes approved. Umbrella labour federation Histadrut says it will fight.
- Search for border patrolmen who abuse Arabs.
- Ultimatum to Netanyahu: Religious parties say either ensure Reform Jews can't be on religious councils via legislation or they'll break up government coalition.
GLOBES
- Bank of Israel, Treasury agree: inflation target 7-9.5 percent.
